_comment: Live error-message suite for the spec-005 nightly quality tier.
Unlike cases.json (the calibration fixture, which carries captured output inline so
the judge could be calibrated before this runner existed), these cases carry only a
COMMAND. The runner executes each against the binary under test and judges whatever
comes back -- so a regression in an error message is caught even though no assertion
Seeded from the human-judgment error steps of docs/qa/smoke-test-plan.md, which is
where a person was previously asked 'is this message actually helpful?'.
`setup` runs in the sandbox before the command. Keep it to file creation: the sandbox
is disposable but the tier must not need network to reach the point of judging.
Every case must FAIL -- a zero exit means the command did not produce the error the
case exists to grade, and the runner reports that as a broken case rather than

cases.why: The most common way a user meets an error: asking for something that isn't installed.
Same class as read_not_found; catches the two paths drifting apart.
A path typo — the message must name the path and the missing SKILL.md.
The directory exists but isn't a skill. Distinct from a missing path, and the message should say so.
Installing by skill id with no repository configured — must say what to configure, not just refuse.

Was known-poor (hit clap's generic E002 unknown-argument path, unnamed, printed twice). `repos skills` now accepts REPOSITORY positionally, so this exercises the domain 'Repository not found' error instead — kept to guard against the parser path regressing.
Type error on a flag — the message should name the value, the flag, and the expected type.
A manifest missing a required section. Exercises the config-validation path rather than the skill-lookup path.
